 item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the next

 Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be received 72 hours prior to
 the day of the Council Meetings.

Inglewood, California
  August 13, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, August 13, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, Finance Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at
  the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority
  Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/
  Parking Authority Chairman/Joint Powers
  Authority  Chairman  Butts,  Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/
  Parking Authority Members/Joint Powers
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor  Agency/Housing  Authority/Finance  Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Cheryl Moore  Management Assistant

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there
  were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, August 8, 2019, in the amount of
  $3,623,609.25, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  register that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 August 13, 2019

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  specific actions be taken on various claim filings.

  A. Reject the following claims in accordance with Government Code Section 913:
  1) Rene Beard for alleged property damage on June 11, 2019.
  2) Mercury Insurance subro Shawnda Burnett for alleged property damage on
  May 31, 2019.
  3) Infinity Insurance subro Sapna Kumar for alleged property damage on April 9,
  2019.
  4) Napoleon Stevens for an alleged refund owed from May 21, 2019.
  5) Idalia Almendarez for an alleged personal injury on December 13, 2018.*
  6) Beverly Paschal for an alleged personal injury on December 17, 2019. *
  B. Reject the following insufficient claim in accordance with Government Code
  Section 913:
  1) Linda Turner for alleged property damage on May 28, 2019.

  * Amended Claim

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Dotson, and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on July 9,
  2019, and July 16, 2019, be approved. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 101  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-077 APPROVED –
  WELFARE TO WORK VOCATIONAL, INTERMEDIARY AND DIRECT
  SERVICES BY AND BETWEEN THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES AND
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD. Staff report dated August 13, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment One to the contract for Welfare-to-Work
  Vocational, Intermediary and Direct Services by and between the County of Los
  Angeles and the City of Inglewood serving as the administrative entity for the
  South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to
  Agreement No. 19-077. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 171  MAYOR TO SIGN PERMITS FOR USE OF INGLEWOOD UNIFIED
  SCHOOL DISTRICT (IUSD) PROPERTIES – AUTHORIZED. Staff report
  dated August 13, 2019, was presented recommending authorization be given to
  the Mayor to sign permits for use of Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD)
  properties for the provisions of the City’s After School Recreation Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby authorize the Mayor to sign permits. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 178  PAYMENT OF INVOICE APPROVED – BEARCOM. Staff report dated
  August 13, 2019, was presented recommending approval to pay an invoice
  submitted by Bearcom for maintenance and repair services of the Police
  Department’s radio infrastructure.

  2
 August 13, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of
  $12,594. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  PURCHASE  APPROVED  –  SULLY-MILLER  CONTRACTING
  COMPANY DBA BLUE DIAMOND MATERIALS. Staff report dated August
  13, 2019, was presented recommending approval to purchase asphalt from Sully-
  Miller Contracting Company dba Blue Diamond Materials.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve cooperative purchase in the
  amount of $85,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  PURCHASE APPROVED – CORE & MAIN, LP. Staff report dated August
  13, 2019, was presented recommending approval to purchase water meters from
  Core & Main, LP.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve cooperative purchase in the
  amount of $80,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 101  FIRST AMENDMENT TO AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT
  NO. 16-155 – APPROVED; MAYOR TO EXECUTE AGREEMENT –
  AUTHORIZED; USE OF TAX-EXEMPT BOND FUNDS – APPROVED.
  Staff report dated August 13, 2019, was presented recommending approval of the
  First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement No. 16-155 approved
  on September 25, 2018 (which was originally dated April 19, 2016), with Pacific
  Coast Elevator Corporation, doing business as Amtech Elevator Services, a
  wholly-owned subsidiary of Otis Elevator Company, increasing the contract
  amount an additional $15,525 (total contract amount of $185,695) to complete the
  modernization of the two elevators at 115 South Locust Street.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, and
  seconded by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Dotson that the City
  Council/Successor Agency does hereby 1) Approve First Amendment to the
  Amended and Restated Agreement No. 16-155; and 2) Authorize the
  Mayor/Chairman to execute the Agreement. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  Franklin, and Mayor/Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by Successor
  Agency Member Franklin that the Successor Agency does hereby approve the use
  of tax-exempt bond funds to fund the remaining outstanding balance of $15,525.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and
  Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 August 13, 2019

 126  DIRECTION REGARDING THE MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS OF 2020.
  Staff report dated August 13, 2019, was presented recommending direction be
  given regarding the Municipal Elections of 2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby direct the City Clerk to inform the
  County Registrar-Recorder’s Office that the City of Inglewood would like to hold
  the General Municipal Election in November 2020 with a Municipal Runoff
  Election in March 2021. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Stuart Bailey thanked Council Member Morales for taking time out of his
  schedule to speak with his neighbor.

  Eric Holly invited everyone out to attend the Chamber of Commerce appreciation
  event for the Police Officers, and Fire Department on September 19, 2019, at the
  Crown Plaza Hotel.

  Willie Agee commented it feels good coming back to Inglewood after being in his
  hometown of Alabama for two weeks.

  Toni William, 17 year home owner, invited Council Member Dotson, and Mayor
  Butts to attend their block club party on 77th Street between 7 & 8th Ave. (Mayor
  Butts obliged)

  Kelly Clark, Attorney for LA Water Keepers, asked the City Council for their
  support opposing the West Basin Water District plan to desalination of the water.

  Speaker Unknown, would like the City Council’s assistance with moving because
  she is being asked to move by her landlord.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned in memory of Gilbert Rodriguez, Pastor Gilbert Chambers, and
  Lonnell Jackson at the hour of 2:23 p.m.

  Approved this 1st day of October, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
